Chapter 6: The Rhythm of Consistency—Showing Up Every Day
Now that we've talked about sharing your work and being real with self-promotion, let’s dive into something that makes all the difference—consistency.
You know, creative growth and getting noticed isn’t about grand, once-in-a-lifetime moments. It’s really about those small things you do, day in and day out. Think of “showing your work” as something you weave into your everyday routine, almost like caring for a garden a little at a time, rather than waiting for that one big harvest.
Here’s the thing—consistency isn’t about forcing yourself into a strict schedule. It’s much more about finding a rhythm that feels natural and sustainable for you. Maybe that means posting a daily sketch, jotting down a quick thought, or even snapping a photo of your workspace. The real magic happens when sharing becomes just another part of your creative flow, not an extra chore on your list.
Picture it like this: building a trail through a forest. Each step might feel tiny, maybe even unimportant. But after a while, you’ll look back and see a clear path—a journey that not only you can be proud of, but one that others can follow, too. This steady presence also shows your audience that you’re reliable, and makes them want to come back and see what’s next.
So, how do you keep this rhythm going? Here are a few simple ideas you might try:
First, set manageable goals. Go for small wins—little acts of sharing that you can actually stick with, instead of biting off more than you can chew.
Next, create rituals. Maybe you share something right after your morning coffee, or just before you settle in for the night. Linking sharing to a habit you already have makes it so much easier.
And don’t be too hard on yourself if you miss a day. Forgive the lapses. Just pick up where you left off, no guilt required.
Imagine a poet who posts just one line or a short stanza each morning. Over time, those little pieces start to add up. Not only do they build a larger body of work, but they also start to attract a community of readers who look forward to each new post.
What’s really interesting is how consistency helps quiet that inner critic. When sharing becomes a habit, it stops feeling like such a big deal. Each post is just another step in the process, which makes it easier to try new things, take chances, and bounce back from mistakes.
In the end, the rhythm of consistency is all about respecting your own creative journey—and letting others be a part of it. It’s that gentle, steady drumbeat that keeps you moving forward, even on days when inspiration feels miles away.
